newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African foreign investment now 30 billion rand.
newsitem.headline: S.African foreign investment now 30 billion rand.

text.p: South Africans have invested about 30 billion rand abroad in assets swaps or direct investments over the last two and a half years, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Tuesday.
Defending the gradual approach to exchange control removal at a parliamentary media briefing, Stals said the Reserve Bank had approved assets swaps worth about 26 billion rand.
"And from the information that we have available, about 16 to 17 billion rand of that has been executed," he said.
At the same time, exchange controls had become more lenient to allow South African companies to make large direct investments abroad.

Total approvals exceeded 15 billion rand for direct investment for the last two and a half years, "So visibly we have given total approval for outside investments of South African funds of more than 30 billion rand," he said.

Asked what South Africa's foreign reserve were and when they would be high enough to completely lift exchange controls, Stals said there was a perception that countries should have enough foreign reserves to cover about three months imports.
"Our present level of reserves at this stage is less than 10 percent of total imports, in other words about five weeks imports, which is far below the world standard of three months." he said.
But South Africa had a fifteen billion rand credit facility that it had not used.
Decisions on lifting exchange controls also depended on future events, Stals said.
"I can't give you one straightforward mathematical answer to say that this is the level of reserves where exchange controls can be lifted," he added.
